# Alibaba, Tencent shares fall on report U.S. weighs curbs on remote AI chip access

Author Ayushman Ojha

Published Nov 12, 2026, 12:14 AM

Alibaba, Tencent shares fall on report U.S. weighs curbs on remote AI chip access

© Reuters.

9988-5.52%

Investing.com -- Shares of Alibaba (HK:9988) and Tencent (HK:0700) fell on Thursday after The Information reported that the U.S. Commerce Department was preparing to finalise rules preventing Chinese AI companies from remotely accessing advanced chips through data centres located overseas.

The proposed measure could be announced this month and would expand existing semiconductor export controls administered by the department's Bureau of Industry and Security to seven additional countries, including Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, the report said.

Hong Kong-listed Alibaba shares fell 5% to HK$95.6 by 05:08 GMT, while Tencent slipped 1.5% to HK$403.6.

The restrictions aim to prevent Chinese companies from accessing advanced processors remotely and curb the smuggling of restricted chips into China.

The report comes amid growing scrutiny of Nvidia's China-related business and Washington's efforts to tighten enforcement of semiconductor export restrictions.

title: Why is Tencent stock falling today? By Investing.com
text:
Published Nov 12, 2026, 01:46 AM

Why is Tencent stock falling today?

© Reuters.

Investing.com -- Tencent Holdings Ltd stock slipped 1.2% to HK$404.8 on Thursday after a report emerged that the U.S. Commerce Department is moving to finalize rules that would prevent Chinese AI companies from remotely accessing advanced semiconductors through data centers located outside China.

The proposed measures, which could be announced as early as this month, would extend existing semiconductor export controls to seven additional countries — including Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand — effectively closing an offshore workaround that Chinese tech giants have relied upon to access cutting-edge AI compute capacity.

The regulatory headline arrives at a particularly sensitive moment for Tencent, which is just days away from reporting its third-quarter earnings on November 18. Analysts at CLSA and Huayuan Securities have flagged that the company’s accelerated AI spending — spanning model training, its WorkBuddy enterprise agent, and the Xiaowei consumer assistant — could pressure Q3 margins.

The broader Hong Kong market was under pressure as well, with the Hang Seng Index declining roughly 0.9% to around 24,092 points by midday, dragged lower by the same chip-access restriction report that hit Tencent. Sector peer Alibaba was a sharper decliner in the same session.

title: Hong Kong Stocks Fall for Second Day
text:
The Hang Seng Index fell 1.2%, or 287 points, to around 22,031 on Thursday, extending losses for a second consecutive session as weakness across technology, retail and financial stocks weighed on the market.

Technology sentiment was pressured by Nvidia’s 8% decline in after-hours US trading following a Wall Street Journal report that the chipmaker was preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang, raising concerns over leadership uncertainty and adding volatility to the global AI sector. Moreover, Hong Kong’s IPO market showed signs of losing steam, with all six companies listing this week pricing shares near the bottom of their marketed ranges amid weak institutional demand.

Investors also remained cautious over US monetary policy following stronger inflation data and increased expectations of a December Federal Reserve rate hike.

Among notable laggards were Tencent (-1.6%), AIA (-0.7%), Meituan (-1.9%), Alibaba (-2.6%), and CK Hutchison (-3.3%).

# Tencent Shares Slid Even Though Profit Rose
Sasha Jovanovic Tue, 10 November 2026 at 10:08 am GMT-5 4 min read
If you had decided on 10 November 2025 to sit out Tencent rather than back the bullish analyst narratives, the outcome over the next twelve months would have felt very different. For Tencent shareholders, the loss over the past year was 35.0%, including dividends. With that drop now on the scoreboard, which of the published growth assumptions, regulatory risks, or AI spending expectations from that starting point most clearly challenged the original optimism?
Tencent is not the only name tied to this theme. Zero in on 53 AI infrastructure stocks and compare how each one is priced.
## The Two Tencent Stories Investors Had To Choose Between
The shares cost HK$650 at the start of the period, so anyone buying Tencent then had to decide which story felt more realistic.
On the bullish side, one analyst framework pointed to a fair value of HK$687, a price implied by assumptions such as 10.5% annual revenue growth and a profit margin moving toward 31.6% over three years as AI and the WeChat ecosystem scaled.
A more cautious Tencent view argued for a fair value of HK$508, based on 12.0% revenue growth, a 24.0% profit margin, and a future P/E of 22.0x over a five year run, with regulatory pressure a central risk.
SEHK:700 1-Year Stock Price Chart ## What The Tencent Results Actually Tested
The clearest update came from Tencent's 2026 Q2 report, where revenue moved from CNY 184,504m to CNY 204,785m and net income edged from CNY 55,628m to CNY 56,022m. Net margin slipped from 30.2% to 27.4%, so the profitability uplift in the bullish HK$687 case went unproven. Overall, the evidence pointed in both directions.
The key assumption to watch here is margin expansion from heavy AI spend. When you assess another tech stock, compare management's promised AI payoff with the reported net margin trend over several quarters, not just the revenue line.
## What Today's Tencent Price Asks You To Believe
Tencent now trades at HK$418, well below where it started one year ago. According to tripledub, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who wrote the Narrative, the Fair Value in that work sits above the current price and rests on cash flows rather than sentiment.
The distinctive claim is that the market prices in long term revenue shrinkage while heavy AI and infrastructure investment is already visible in the cash flow line. Anyone buying today would need to judge whether that elevated capex eventually earns enough to cover depreciation from these projects.

China stocks edged up on semiconductor gains, but Hong Kong shares dropped due to Alibaba's chip spin-off and CK Hutchison's paused listing, reflecting a disappointing year for Chinese equities.

- Alibaba's chip business spin-off and its effect on Hong Kong's Hang Seng.
- CK Hutchison's decision to pause the AS Watson Group dual listing.
- Factors contributing to the disappointing performance of Chinese equities this year.

 By Reuters 

HONG KONG: China stocks inched higher on Thursday, buoyed by semiconductor gains, while Hong Kong shares extended losses as heavyweights Alibaba and CK Hutchison weighed. 

China’s blue-chip CSI300 Index edged up 0.1% by the lunch break, while the Shanghai Composite Index rose 0.2%.

Hong Kong’s benchmark Hang Seng was down 0.9%.

Alibaba Group dropped 5% by midday after the tech and e-commerce giant said it is pushing ahead with the spin-off of its chip business T-Head, dragging the Hang Seng Tech down 1.4%.

The sell-off also comes amid muted expectations for this year’s Singles’ Day shopping festival as consumers tighten their purse strings.

Hong Kong conglomerate CK Hutchison lost more than 4% after it reportedly paused a planned dual listing of retailer AS Watson Group. In mainland A-shares, semiconductor and AI-related stocks outperformed, tracking overnight Wall Street gains.

Gold and robotics shares led the decline, on the other hand.

Larry Hu, Macquarie Group’s chief China economist, said Chinese equities’ performance has been “disappointing” so far this year, largely due to the lack of stimulus policy to support domestic demand.

Going into 2027, the strength of exports “will determine how much domestic stimulus Beijing will provide to meet the GDP growth target” and then drive the performance of Chinese equities, he said in a note.

The smaller Shenzhen index was up 0.08%, the start-up board ChiNext Composite index was higher by 0.06% and Shanghai’s tech-focused STAR50 index was up 2.35%.

HONG KONG, Nov. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Tencent joined Hong Kong FinTech Week x StartmeupHK 2026, sharing how it is deepening global payment interoperability and applying AI across financial services through product showcases and executive panels.

"We are the first in China to propose a payment ontology model, and run it on one of the largest payment networks," Lin said, adding that the ontology model is like a smart map of the payment world, which automatically detects the abnormal traffic. title: Tencent stock enters earnings week as AI rollout raises stakes
author: Rafael Müller
text:
Published on 11/09/2026 at 09:26 | Editorial responsibility: Rafael Müller,

Tencent stock enters the final stretch before November 18 results as investors weigh AI spending against growth. Hy4 adds vision and computer-use tools to Tencent's product ecosystem.

## AI rollout meets an earnings test

- Tencent will publish its third-quarter results on November 18.
- Hy4 adds visual understanding and computer-use capabilities to Tencent's AI ecosystem.
- Tencent's internal tests ranked Hy4 first among the open-source models included in its financial benchmark.

 

 

Tencent Holdings Ltd., KYG875721634, Illustration mit AI erstellt.

Tencent is heading into its November 18 earnings release with artificial intelligence at the center of the investment debate. Invezz reported on Monday that Tencent's upcoming results are a key catalyst for Hong Kong-listed technology stocks after a year in which the company has faced slower growth and higher operating costs.

Tencent stock traded at 47.74 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 09:17 CET on Monday, November 9, 2026. The quote provides a current trading indication, while the earnings release will offer the next major test of revenue growth, profitability and investment needs.

## Hy4 broadens Tencent's AI push

On November 4, Tencent announced the release of Hy4, the latest model from its Hunyuan AI team. In its official release, the company said Hy4 adds visual understanding and computer-use capabilities for command-line and graphical interfaces. Tencent also highlighted applications in WorkBuddy, financial analysis, software development and scientific research.

The model is designed to connect with workplace information in WorkBuddy and WeCom, including chats, emails, documents, calendars and meetings. Tencent said its WorkBuddy evaluation produced an average score of 83.18 and a 96.15 percent task pass rate, with Hy4 ranking first in nine of 12 mainland Chinese scenarios.

Tencent's financial benchmark involved 213 professionals and 579 real-world tasks. Hy4 scored 3.04, ahead of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 at 2.97 and Kimi K3.1 Pro and GLM-5.3 at 2.68. The figures are Tencent's own internal or company-led evaluations, so their investment significance will depend on adoption, usage and monetization rather than benchmark performance alone.

## Results will test investment intensity

The November 18 report should show how Tencent's AI expansion is affecting the broader business. Invezz said Tencent raised 5.7 billion US dollars in October to support investment. That financing highlights the scale of the capital required to build AI infrastructure, while the results may clarify whether gaming, advertising and enterprise services are generating enough operating momentum to absorb the additional spending.

For shareholders, the key questions are whether AI tools can strengthen Tencent's software ecosystem, how quickly enterprise use converts into revenue and whether higher infrastructure costs pressure near-term margins. Hy4's integration into products such as WorkBuddy, CodeBuddy and Tencent Cloud gives the company several routes to commercialization, but the November report remains the first scheduled checkpoint for financial effects.

title: HSBC explores Singapore base to reduce China reliance | The Straits Times
text:
# HSBC explores bolstering Singapore to balance China reliance

HSBC’s review highlights how some of the world’s largest financial groups are moving to insulate their Asian assets from mounting geopolitical risks.

 PHOTO: REUTERS

Published Nov 12, 2026, 11:40 AM

Updated Nov 12, 2026, 12:11 PM

- HSBC is exploring ways to make its Singapore business more independent to reduce reliance on China and Hong Kong. The project is called “Project Sirena”.
- The bank plans to combine its main Singapore banking units first. It may later move other regional operations there, creating a second Asian base alongside Hong Kong.
- HSBC says there are no firm decisions yet and no plan to change its Hong Kong-led structure. The move could upset regulators and Beijing, while Singapore gains as a stable wealth hub.

HSBC Holdings has been exploring ways to ease its reliance on China including Hong Kong and give more independence to its Singapore operations, as the bank seeks to diversify risk across its Asia business, according to people familiar with the matter.

The London-based lender, which generated about 40% of its pretax profit in the first half from Hong Kong, has internally discussed several options to give its Singapore arm greater autonomy, the people said, asking not to be identified discussing a private matter. The initiative is being carried out under the name “Project Sirena”.

HSBC’s review highlights how some of the world’s largest financial groups are moving to insulate their Asian assets from mounting geopolitical risks. Singapore, bolstered by relative political stability and its standing as a premier wealth and banking hub, has emerged as a top beneficiary as firms look beyond Greater China for operational flexibility. 

It comes even as Chief Executive Officer Georges Elhedery has repeatedly voiced confidence in Hong Kong’s prospects, predicting the city would overtake Switzerland to

...

In a first step, HSBC plans to combine its major banking services in Singapore under one entity over the next few years. A possible next move would be to bring in the other regional operations under the Singapore subsidiary, with the ultimate goal of establishing a second regional base alongside Hong Kong, according to the people.

In a statement, Surendra Rosha, co-CEO of Asia and the Middle East, confirmed the bank will combine its separate units in Singapore as part of a simplification drive, though said it had no further plans after that.

“All of our Asia-Pacific banking entities remain under the ownership and management of the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited subsidiary head officed in Hong Kong, and there is no plan to make any changes to this,” Rosha said in an e-mailed statement.

The deliberations remain fluid with no firm decisions on the path forward, the people said. Like other multinationals, HSBC is also wary of appearing to hedge its bets, given its significant exposure in Greater China and concerns about provoking regulators, the people said. HSBC shares fell as much as 0.8% in early Hong Kong trading.

Making its Singapore operations more independent would be a major step for the 161-year-old lender, which was founded in Hong Kong and moved its headquarters to London in 1993.

At the same time, the bank is becoming more reliant on the Chinese territory after announcing in 2025 a US$14 billion (S$18 billion) takeover of partly owned Hang Seng Bank, while it has also exited businesses in Europe and the Americas.

Any signs of hedging Hong Kong, where HSBC serves as one of three currency-issuing lenders, would face stiff local pushback. It would also risk alienating Beijing, where the bank maintains expansive mainland operations.

...

Hong Kong remains HSBC’s profit engine, generating US$7.8 billion of pretax profits in the first half of 2026, about 40% of the group total. Singapore, despite its growing importance as an Asian wealth hub, generated just US$774 million – roughly a 10th of Hong Kong’s profit. India contributed US$965 million and mainland China US$1.8 billion, according to HSBC’s accounts. BLOOMBERG

For Hong Kong homeowners, the number that matters is not HIBOR. The HKAB one-month fixing was about 2.59% on Tuesday.  Published on 11/05/2026 at 12:00 | Editorial responsibility: Rafael Müller, Editor-in-Chief AD HOC NEWS 

HSBC stock faces a mixed earnings picture after revenue fell short of consensus. The bank kept its 2026 targets and plans another 1 billion US dollar buyback.

## Profit growth meets capital returns

- HSBC increased third-quarter pretax profit despite revenue below consensus.
- Management retained its 2026 targets and approved a third interim dividend.
- A further share buyback could bring total announced repurchases to 2 billion US dollars for the year.

 

 

HSBC, GB0005405286, Illustration mit AI erstellt.

HSBC Holdings reported stronger third-quarter earnings on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, but revenue fell short of the consensus compiled by the bank. A CNBC report said pretax profit rose 32 percent from a year earlier to 9.6 billion US dollars, while revenue increased from 17.8 billion to 18.6 billion US dollars.

## Revenue miss tempers profit advance

The result was broadly in line with expectations on profit. Pretax profit came in at 9.63 billion US dollars against a 9.69 billion US dollar consensus estimate, while revenue missed the 18.93 billion US dollar forecast. Banking net interest income rose 6 percent to 9.3 billion US dollars, supported by deposit growth and reinvestment of the structural hedge at higher yields.

The reported profit comparison also benefited from the absence of 1.4 billion US dollars in legal provisions recorded a year earlier. Operating expenses fell 12 percent year on year to 8.8 billion US dollars, although HSBC said expenses excluding notable items increased amid inflation and higher technology spending. The bank's return on tangible equity reached 18.8 percent for the first nine months excluding notable items, according to the company.

## Buyback and dividend support returns

HSBC approved a third interim dividend of 0.10 US dollars per share and plans another share buyback of up to 1 billion US dollars. The bank completed a previous 1 billion US dollar repurchase on September 28 and expects the new programme to finish before the full-year 2026 results. The capital-return plans support the bank's stated preference for dividends and buybacks while leaving room for organic investment.

Management retained its main targets. HSBC continues to expect banking net interest income of at least 46 billion US dollars in 2026 and targets return on tangible equity of at least 17 percent through 2028, excluding notable items. It also expects revenue to grow each year through 2028, reaching 5 percent growth in 2028 compared with 2027 on a constant-currency basis. The dividend payout target remains 50 percent of earnings per share excluding material notable items and related impacts.

## HSBC stock tracks the earnings balance

text:
港股科网股走势分化美团独跌近6% 电商增长焦虑升温引关注

2026-11-09 15:19 星期一 财联社 冯轶 

财联社11月9日讯（编辑 冯轶）港股互联网板块今日走势分化，一众科网股中，美团日内大幅下挫近6%，引发市场关注。

消息面上，有媒体报道称，摩根士丹利最新发布的研究将美团评级下调至“与大市同步”，目标价则从110港元下调至90港元，降幅接近两成，成为美团股价走跌的导火索。

此外，拼多多、同程旅行、快手等互联网企业也均遭遇目标价下调。

大摩研究指出，电商行业正进入结构性低增长阶段，预计2026至2030年平台商品交易总额的复合年增长率仅有3.2%，到2030年会放缓至2.6%。而与此同时，持续的竞争可能会消耗市场期待的“成熟红利”。

值得一提的是，有数据显示，截至2026年9月，美团与阿里日均外卖单量合计接近1.4亿单，双方订单量比例稳定在约4:6，阿里相较外卖补贴战前约2:7的比例明显提升。此外，近日豆包也官宣正式接入抖音生活服务，或意味着美团在本地生活领域的核心主营业务将继续面临高强度竞争。

另一方面，据国家统计局数据显示，10月份，食品烟酒及在外餐饮类价格同比下降1.6%。也影响了市场对电商板块的短线情绪。

国信证券表示，宏观层面消费需求仍在磨底，商品、服务消费均显乏力。华泰证券也分析称，10月社零总额同比增速或从9月的1.1%回落至0%。

不过，也有分析指出，随着双十一电商大促临近，以及圣诞、元旦和春节前的备货与出行需求叠加，多个消费场景有望迎来集中释放。叠加“扩内需、促服务消费”等政策持续发力，电商行业也或出现阶段性的情绪催化窗口。

1、背景补充 近期港股互联网板块因机构评级调整出现显著波动，美团股价大幅下挫成为焦点。摩根士丹利下调美团至“与大市同步”评级，目标价从110港元降至90港元，降幅近两成，并指出电商行业进入结构性低增长阶段，预计2026至2030年平台商品交易总额复合年增长率仅为3.2%。竞争加剧导致“成熟红利”被消耗，阿里在外卖市场份额显著提升，且抖音生活服务接入豆包进一步加剧本地生活赛道竞争。同时，宏观数据显示10月食品烟酒及餐饮价格同比下降1.6%，社零增速预期回落，反映消费需求仍在磨底。 2、影响分析 首先，估值逻辑重构。机构下调目标价反映出市场对互联网巨头高增长预期的修正，投资者需警惕依赖流量红利的企业面临估值中枢下移风险，尤其是那些护城河受竞争侵蚀的标的。其次，行业分化加剧。在存量博弈背景下，具备强运营能力、成本控制优势及新业务突破点的企业更具韧性，而单纯依靠补贴扩张的模式难以为继。再次，短期情绪与长期基本面背离。尽管双十一等大促节点可能带来阶段性交易机会，但宏观消费乏力制约了反弹高度。投资策略上，建议回避高位震荡的传统科网股，关注受益于政策促消费及服务消费转型的新兴细分领域，同时密切跟踪头部企业在AI应用落地及国际化拓展方面的进展，以捕捉结构性阿尔法收益。 （以上内容由AI生成，不构成投资建议，不代表刊登平台观点，请独立判断和决策。）

Hong Kong shares narrowed early gains to close the morning trading session up 49 points.

The Morgan Stanley report noted that China’s e-commerce industry is entering a phase of structural low growth, with platform gross merchandise value forecast to grow at a compound annual growth rate of only 3.2 percent from 2026 to 2030, slowing to 2.6 percent by 2030.

Unlike typical mature industries, China’s e-commerce sector shows almost no signs of consolidation, with cash-rich platforms continuing to defend their core businesses while entering competitors’ markets.

title: Xiaomi Buyback Fails to Offset Rate-Driven Slide as Daiwa Lifts Target to HK$35
author: Rafael Müller
text:
Xiaomi shares fell 3.0% to €3.37 amid rate worries. The company bought back 1.66 million Class B shares, and Daiwa raised its target to HK$35.

 

 

Xiaomi Buyback Fails to Offset Rate-Driven Slide as Daiwa Lifts Target to HK$35 Illustration mit AI erstellt.

Xiaomi's shares fell 3.0% on Thursday to €3.37 as renewed global interest-rate worries weighed on Hong Kong's technology sector. Reuters attributed the broader decline in the Hang Seng Tech Index to stronger-than-expected US inflation data and mounting expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike, which pressured tech names across the board. Tencent, Meituan and Alibaba were among the stocks caught in the downdraft.

## Buyback Programme Continues

Against that backdrop, the smartphone and EV maker returned to the market with another round of share purchases. Xiaomi bought back 1.66 million Class B shares on the Hong Kong exchange, spending roughly HK$49.9 million, according to a regulatory filing. The repurchases came at prices between HK$30.08 and HK$30.24 apiece. The move follows a similar transaction on Monday, when the company also acquired about 1.66 million Class B shares for around HK$49.9 million.

## Daiwa Raises Target, Reaffirms Buy

Analysts, meanwhile, are growing more optimistic. Daiwa lifted its price target on Xiaomi from HK$30 to HK$35 on November 3 while keeping its buy rating on the stock.

The company also reported progress on the robotics front that same day. According to Xiaomi, a humanoid robot completed its first eight-hour work shift at an automobile plant. A separate embodied foundation model was put through trial operations at a Xiaomi residential complex.

## India Manufacturing Talks at Exploratory Stage

On the production side, Xiaomi is scouting local partners in India for planned household-appliance manufacturing, The Economic Times reported. The discussions remain in an exploratory phase, with the company focused on finding local production capacity in the country.

## Board to Review Q3 on November 24

Investors now have a firm date for the next set of numbers. Xiaomi's board will meet on November 24, 2026, to review and approve the unaudited consolidated results for the third quarter and the nine months ended September 30, 2026. The agenda covers both the standalone quarter and the year-to-date period.

title: Xiaomi Trims Buyback Tab While BofA Cuts Q3 Revenue View
author: Rafael Müller
text:
Xiaomi repurchased 1.66 million B-shares for HK$49.9 million, set up an auto international unit, and plans RMB 200 billion in R&D over five years.

 

 

Xiaomi Trims Buyback Tab While BofA Cuts Q3 Revenue View Illustration mit AI erstellt.

Xiaomi bought back 1.66 million B-shares on the Hong Kong exchange, spending HK$49.9 million according to media reports, with the repurchased stock set to be cancelled. The execution prices ranged from HK$30.08 to HK$30.24 per share, and the stock was down 1.2% in today's session.

The buyback lands alongside a flurry of corporate activity. On Thursday, Xiaomi disclosed the issue of roughly 1.6 million B-shares from exercised employee options, drawn from its monthly report on securities movements for October. The company received USD 402,529 from that issuance.

## Overseas Push for the Car Business

Xiaomi Auto has set up an international business unit and named Vice President Yu Liguo as its general manager, media reports said Friday. The new division covers international sales and market development, and also takes in delivery and customer service.

That overseas build-out comes as the EV arm rides a strong run at home. Xiaomi reported more than 50,000 electric vehicles delivered in October — the highest monthly figure of the year, per Reuters. Cumulative deliveries from January through October reached about 336,000 vehicles, against a full-year target of 550,000 for 2026.

On the handset side, Xiaomi said on its official X account on November 2 that the Xiaomi 18 Pro series will launch globally in November.

...

Manufacturing is getting attention too. Media reports on Wednesday said Xiaomi showed humanoid robots working an eight-hour shift at its own car plant for the first time, sorting trim parts for vehicle assembly. The robots took two charging breaks during the stint, with a reported total duration of eight hours and five minutes.

Separate reports on November 3 described tests of Xiaomi robots in a Xiaomi residential complex, covering more than 30 minutes of autonomous work and over 50 household tasks. Those trials complemented the reported deployment in the assembly area of the car plant.

## R&D Budget and a Trimmed Forecast

Vice President and CMO Xu Fei said at the World Media Summit on Saturday that Xiaomi plans to spend RMB 200 billion on research and development over the next five years. More than RMB 105.5 billion flowed into the area over the past five years, according to company figures. Xu also discussed the use of Xiaomi technology and its connected ecosystem in media communication.

Bank of America reaffirmed its buy rating on Xiaomi on November 2 but cut its Q3 2026 revenue estimate by 6% to 105 billion yuan. The bank cited subdued IoT demand in China and electric vehicle deliveries falling short of expectations as the drags.

Xiaomi stock dropped 3.0% to EUR 3.37 amid global rate anxiety. Daiwa raised its target to HK$35, and Xiaomi kept buying back shares.

 

 

Xiaomi Sinks With Hong Kong Tech Peers as Buyback and Daiwa Upgrade Fail to Halt Slide Illustration mit AI erstellt.

Xiaomi's stock came under pressure for a second straight session as renewed global interest-rate anxiety rippled through Hong Kong's technology sector. The shares fell 3.0% on the day to EUR 3.37, extending a 2.7% decline from the previous session that had already dragged the stock lower alongside Tencent, Alibaba, Meituan and JD.com.

Reuters attributed the broader retreat in the Hang Seng Tech Index to resurgent concerns over global borrowing costs. Stronger-than-expected US inflation data, combined with mounting expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise rates, weighed on Hong Kong-listed technology names, according to the report.

## Buyback Program Rolls On

Against that difficult tape, Xiaomi continued to support its own stock. The company repurchased 1.66 million B-shares on the Hong Kong exchange, spending roughly HK$49.9 million, according to a mandatory disclosure. The buyback follows a similar move on Monday, when Xiaomi also acquired its own shares for HK$49.9 million. The repurchased stock is slated for cancellation.

## Daiwa Lifts Target, Reiterates Buy

Analysts, for their part, remain constructive. Daiwa raised its price target on Xiaomi to HK$35 from HK$30 on November 3, while reaffirming its buy rating on the shares.

The company also reported progress on the robotics front that same day. According to Xiaomi, a humanoid robot completed an eight-hour work shift at an automobile plant for the first time. In addition, an embodied foundation model was put through trial operations at a Xiaomi residential complex.

## October Deliveries Top 50,000

In the automotive business, the China Passenger Car Association recorded 50,123 vehicle deliveries for October 2026. Xiaomi itself had announced on November 1 that deliveries had exceeded 50,000 units.

Separately, the company is exploring local partnerships in India for the manufacture of home appliances, according to a report in the Economic Times. Those plans remain in an early review phase, the newspaper said, with Xiaomi sounding out potential local partners for production in the country.

## Board to Sign Off on Q3

Investors now turn to the November 24 board meeting, at which directors will review and approve Xiaomi's unaudited consolidated results for the third quarter of 2026. The meeting will also cover the company's results for the nine months ending September 30, 2026.

title: Xiaomi shares climb as October EV deliveries top 50,000 By Investing.com
author: Ayushman Ojha
text:
# Xiaomi shares climb as October EV deliveries top 50,000

Author Ayushman Ojha

Published 02/11/2026, 05:22

© Reuters

1810 0.00%

Investing.com-- Xiaomi (HK:1810) shares rose on Monday after the Chinese smartphone maker said its electric vehicle deliveries exceeded 50,000 in October, marking their highest monthly level so far this year as the company ramps up production to meet its annual target.

Hong Kong-listed shares of the company rose 6.3% to HK$28.14 by 05:12 GMT.

The company delivered about 336,490 vehicles in the first 10 months of 2026, representing roughly 61% of its full-year target of 550,000 vehicles.

Monthly deliveries rose from more than 30,000 in August to over 40,000 in September before crossing 50,000 in October.

The October milestone was only the second time Xiaomi’s monthly deliveries had exceeded 50,000, following December 2025, when it delivered 50,212 vehicles.

Xiaomi is expanding its vehicle business as it seeks to diversify beyond smartphones and compete in China’s crowded electric vehicle market.

title: Xiaomi Buyback and Beijing IoT Paper Fail to Shield Stock From Rate Squeeze
author: Rafael Müller
text:
Xiaomi repurchased 1.66M Class B shares for about HK$49.9M as its stock fell 2.1%; it is also reviewing early-stage India appliance manufacturing.

 

 

Xiaomi Buyback and Beijing IoT Paper Fail to Shield Stock From Rate Squeeze Illustration mit AI erstellt.

Xiaomi spent roughly HK$49.9 million buying back 1.66 million Class B ordinary shares, the company disclosed, with the repurchased stock earmarked for cancellation. The shares changed hands at between HK$29.96 and HK$30.12 apiece.

The buyback landed on a rough day for Hong Kong's technology complex. Xiaomi's stock shed 2.1% to €3.40 as global yields climbed and expectations of further rate hikes hardened. The Economic Times groups the company with Hong Kong tech names squeezed by hotter US inflation, and the Hang Seng Tech Index itself gave up 1.4% over the session.

## India Manufacturing Under Review

Away from the trading floor, Xiaomi is sounding out local partners to make household appliances in India. The Economic Times reports the review is still at an early stage, with potential suppliers only now being evaluated.

## Open IoT Paper With Peking University

The company also published an industry-open whitepaper on IoT device models together with Peking University yesterday. Xiaomi says it is contributing technical experience drawn from more than 1.16 billion AIoT devices for the wider sector. The partners presented the paper at the CCF China Software Conference, focusing on the device model underpinning the Internet of Things — the networking of connected devices.

Robotics work has advanced in parallel. On 3 November Xiaomi reported that a humanoid robot had, for the first time, staffed a sorting station at one of its own car plants for eight continuous hours. A trial of household chores in Xiaomi youth apartments also got under way.

## All Four Models on Premium Sales Board

In the auto business, founder and CEO Lei Jun said yesterday that all four Xiaomi models appeared in China's October sales ranking for vehicles priced above 200,000 yuan. Reuters puts deliveries of electric vehicles at about 336,000 units from January through October, with the company targeting 550,000 shipments for 2026.

Analysts are less upbeat on the near term. UOB Kay Hian forecast on 2 November a 6.7% year-on-year decline in third-quarter 2026 revenue to RMB 106 billion, with weaker IoT and EV sales expected to outweigh a stronger smartphone quarter.

## Board to Sign Off on Q3

The board is due to review and approve unaudited consolidated results on 24 November 2026, covering both the third quarter of 2026 and the nine months to 30 September 2026 — a single sitting that clears the standalone quarter and the cumulative nine-month figures together. The date matches the HKEX calendar entry for the Q3 2026 release.

title: Xiaomi stock gains as Xetra move sharpens November 24 earnings test
author: Rafael Müller
text:
Xiaomi stock traded higher on Tuesday as investors looked toward the November 24 results. CICC retained its Buy rating and set a HKD 34.00 target.

## What Xiaomi investors should watch

- Xiaomi faces a November 24 review of unaudited third-quarter and nine-month results.
- CICC retained its Buy rating while the June-quarter comparison showed lower revenue and net profit year over year.
- Investors will assess whether vehicle expansion can improve profitability without worsening pressure on smartphones and smart hardware.

 

 

Xiaomi Corp., KYG9830T1067, Illustration mit AI erstellt.

Xiaomi stock traded at 3.46 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 15:34 CET on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, 1.47 percent above the Xetra close of Monday. The move keeps the focus on Xiaomi's next earnings test, scheduled for November 24.

AD HOC NEWS reported that CICC maintained its Buy rating on November 3 and set a HKD 34.00 price target. The analyst view came as investors weighed Xiaomi's smartphone business against its expanding electric-vehicle operations.

## Growth still faces a profit test

Xiaomi's second-quarter revenue fell to HKD 108.46 billion from HKD 115.96 billion a year earlier, while net profit declined to HKD 9.42 billion from HKD 11.90 billion. The figures cover the quarter ended June 30 and show that vehicle expansion has not yet translated into stronger group revenue or profit.

The November 24 release will give investors a clearer view of vehicle economics, smartphone demand and the cost of Xiaomi's broader product push. The key question is whether higher vehicle volumes can be accompanied by improving profitability while the smartphone and smart-hardware businesses remain resilient.

title: Why is Xiaomi stock surging today? By Investing.com
text:
© Reuters.

Investing.com -- Xiaomi stock surged 6.3% to HK$28.14 today after the company’s electric vehicle division disclosed October deliveries of more than 50,000 units, marking the strongest monthly performance of 2026 and only the second time in the company’s EV history that monthly shipments have cleared that level.

The delivery beat was amplified by a fresh analyst endorsement: Citi reiterated its "Buy" rating on the stock with a target price of HK$33.2, arguing that the delivery data supports short-term share price stability and that the current valuation represents an attractive entry point, particularly as a defensive position during broader AI-driven market swings.

The broader Hong Kong market provided a constructive backdrop, with the Hang Seng Index climbing 0.61% and the Hang Seng Tech Index advancing 2.85% by midday. Hong Kong shares rebounded after logging deep losses in October on a wipeout in technology valuations.
